acceptanceClaims: naive compensation-applied and compensation-not-applied histories produced different evaluator-private balances but byte-equivalent sender ledgers and byte-equivalent caller recovery views, forcing UNKNOWN
restricted UID-65534 callers were physically denied downstream private balance reads while retaining the public compensation invocation capability
blind replay of the naive subtract-one compensation overcompensated the already-repaired hidden history from 1 to 0 while correctly repairing the hidden unrepaired history from 2 to 1
the repeat-safe candidate used a distinct request/effect/capability/effectType identity with retrySemantics=convergent-repair-duplicate

under the idempotent compensation protocol the caller views remained byte-equivalent and historically UNKNOWN, but same-protocol retry returned already-repaired for hidden balance 1 and applied for hidden balance 2, converging both to 1
all downstream private worlds physically contained only balance.json, all public local endpoints closed to zero, and no IP network or external target was consumed
limitations: the downstream private state remains durable, single-host and internally readable by the compensation authority
loss, corruption, fork or partition of downstream private truth remains untested
multi-resource, cross-party, concurrent and distributed compensation remain unproved
the experiment does not establish generic exactly-once, saga or transaction semantics
